pairs.subject: cross-provider-benchmark-operations
pairs.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:132 The model-arm scorecard reports quality and output tokens but no latency or priced cost, although engine.ts captures durationMs and costUsd on the same calls, so the three-axis trade-off the standard requires cannot be read off the artifact.

techniques.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:132 Arms are declared in a table (ARMS / ARM_CFG), but each target reports quality and tokens only, with no latency median/tail or priced cost. The gold arm (opus) also grades its own family without a recorded warning.

scripts/hybrid-bench/engine.ts:11 Reasoning effort is a separate typed field in RunOpts and in every arm config ({model, effort}). It is not a suffix on the model string, so it can be varied independently.
scripts/hybrid-bench/engine.ts:30 The CLI path pins no temperature or seed, and no run or row records a determinism stamp. derived.ts has a --repeats flag but never stamps its output.
scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:40 Cases are the first N rows of a live rows file, with no stratification, no frozen or versioned dataset id, and no dataset version in the output JSON.
scripts/hybrid-bench/engine.ts:38 An opt-in metered API-key path exists, but nowhere is there a pre-flight estimate, a ceiling, or a 'partial' marker on a halted run.

scripts/hybrid-bench/derived.ts:118 The engine runs on subscription OAuth, a purchased allowance. Any CLI failure, quota exhaustion included, is logged as a generic error and skipped, yet N still counts the skipped cell, so a missing cell is scored as a miss.
scripts/hybrid-bench/engine.ts:100 Cost and duration are captured in RunResult but no scorecard or JSON artifact surfaces them. Skipped-cell caveats are also missing from the rendered card.

scripts/hybrid-bench/agg.ts:126 Narrate arms were handed the deterministic tally. Their row prints '— (given)' instead of the 100% they would otherwise show, so the advantage is disclosed in the row itself.
scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:138 The card closes with a token-savings figure, not with low-score cases clustered by pattern or concrete recommendations.
scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:10 The benchmark asks the cheapest-sufficient question but answers it by eyeballing point estimates, with no test of 'not significantly worse' and no priced-cost frontier.
scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:13 These are hand-run offline CLI experiments that do not share a process with ingestion, so there is no claimable queue to require.
scripts/hybrid-bench/engine.ts:26 The only engine is the hosted Claude CLI, and no locally served model appears in any arm.
